symptom: On the **legacy** engine (MXCLI_ENGINE=legacy), `create or modify workflow` that does not restate stored event handlers / boundary events / nested Ends / AI agent tasks / completion rules is written ("Created workflow") and deletes them, while the default modelsdk engine refuses the same statement with the guard-don't-drop list
cause: The workflow rewrite guards walk `ctx.Backend.GetRawUnit` with type switches on `map[string]any` / `[]any`. The legacy backend decodes with mongo-driver v1 `bson.Unmarshal` into map[string]any, which yields nested documents as map[string]any but ARRAYS AS `primitive.A` — a named type a `case []any` does not match. So every guard saw no list at all (measured with a probe: `OnWorkflowEvent primitive.A`, `Flow map[string]interface {}`). The modelsdk reader normalizes to plain slices (`modelsdk/mpr/reader_raw.go normalizeBSONValue`), which is why only legacy was blind
insight: A guard tested only with hand-built `[]any` fixtures proves nothing about the legacy engine: build the fixture, then `bson.Marshal` + `bson.Unmarshal` into map[string]any to get the shape legacy's GetRawUnit really returns (`legacyShaped` in validate_workflow_rewrite_legacy_test.go). Normalized in the guard, not in MprBackend.GetRawUnit, because catalog (`builder_regularexpressions.go`) asserts `bson.A` on raw units. Found only by running the e2e rewrite on BOTH engines — the modelsdk run was green. Other `[]any`-only raw walkers (REST body guard, queued-call guard) are suspects of the same class. Control: normalizer returning its input fails the legacy-shape tests
